reading.ours: two units of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — an instrument check, and it is printed first because nothing below it means anything until it passes. The true ratio is a little UNDER 2: both sides pay the driving loop once, so the exact expectation is (2u + L) / (u + L) with L the loop and u one unit, which at sixteen dependent steps per unit puts it around 1.9. A reading below 1.5 means this process could not resolve a deliberate doubling, and the runner voids the report rather than printing prices under it.

reading.ours: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: the same body again, over its own copy of the same state
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — the noise floor. The two sides are identical code over identical, separately-allocated state, so the true ratio is 1.00 exactly and every departure from it printed here was produced by this machine at this moment. The rule that follows is the one the whole table is read under: NO RATIO CLOSER TO 1.00 THAN THIS GAP IS A READING. It also bounds the per-row noise figure, which is the same idea measured again inside every pair — each pair times its floor twice, once before our side and once after, and prints how far the two disagreed.

reading.ours: re-file a row under 2 addresses — two linear scans through the store's own comparison
reading.floor: the same re-file, diffed through a Set of the 2 keys
reading.caveat: 2 ADDRESSES PER ROW. Ours is O(A²) word comparisons and no allocation; the floor is O(A) with two `Set`s allocated per write. THE CROSSOVER IS THE CLAIM this family exists to check, and it is the one thing the shared cost cannot distort: the write, the frame and the selector are identical on both halves, so they add the same constant to both numbers — which pulls each RATIO toward 1.00 but leaves the size at which the two designs are equal exactly where it was. Read the family, not the row. WHAT THE SET BUYS is that it does not degrade: at some size the scans lose and keep losing. WHAT IT GIVES UP is not nanoseconds — the scans ask the STORE whether a bucket is addressed by a key, so an index filed by a chain of identities is served by the shipped design and cannot be served by this floor at all, which is why this floor is writable only over a keyed store. Every timed operation leaves the address list unchanged, which is the steady state both designs are written for; the floor delegates the leaves and the joins of a CHANGED list to the shipped code, and no timed operation takes that branch.
